subject: seasonality in simple DLM through dummies (no indicator function used)

messages.author: 83d59c07601a6f59
messages.subject: seasonality in simple DLM through dummies (no indicator function used)
parts:
Hi all,

I'm trying to fit a univariate DLM with montly seasonality for a daily dataset so I decided to use 12 dummies with RStan. I have created a vector 'dum' which picks the index of the month for each observation that I use as if were an indicator function for the seasonality parameters 'alpha'. I have tried many alternatives with the system equations however I haven't been able to speed it up. See attached my code and data.

Many thanks for helping us,
Antonio

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] seasonality in simple DLM through dummies (no indicator function used)
parts:
Here's the model. Comments below.

======================================
data {
int<lower=0> N;
real y[N]; // data
int<lower=1> J;
int<lower=1> S;
int<lower=1> dum[N]; // monthly dummies
}
parameters {
real theta[N];
real mu[N];
real phi;
real alpha[S];
real<lower=0> sigma_inv[J];
}

The way to speed this up is to vectorize.

model {

// priors
mu[1] ~ normal( 4000 , 1.0e+4 );
theta[1] ~ normal( 4000 , 1.0e+4 );
y[1] ~ normal( alpha[ dum[1] ] + theta[1] , 1/sigma_inv[1] ) ;

// likelihood
for (t in 2:N) {
mu[t] ~ normal( mu[t-1] , 1/sigma_inv[3] );
theta[t] ~ normal( mu[t] + phi*theta[ t - 1 ] , 1/sigma_inv[2] );
y[t] ~ normal( theta[t] + alpha[ dum[t] ] , 1/sigma_inv[1] ) ;
}

}

===============================

* I'd add upper=S to dum and rename it --- it's an indicator, not a dummy.

* There's an improper uniform prior on sigma_inv and then it's inverted to
get sigma --- not sure why it's done this way. Priors can help control inference.

* If you must use this sigma_inv parameterization, at least only convert
sigma_inv once, either by assigning to a local and reusing or by vectorizing

* The biggest speedup will come from vectorizing; you can use the vector
slicing functions, e.g., replacing the loop with:

tail(mu,N-1) ~ normal(head(mu,N-1), 1 / sigma_inv[3]);

I should put an example like this in the manual

* Given the location scale of mu and theta (mean 4000, sd of 1000), it
might help to provide your own initializations

* Is 1e4 a realistic value for mu[1] and theta[1]? if not, choosing tighter
priors can help control computation

* priors on all the coefficients alpha and phi may also help control inference --- you
can tell if you have problems looking at traceplots with extreme values

- Bob

parts:
Sorry --- that's not going to work.

You'll need to create the means in a loop. That'll still be
faster than calling normal in a loop.

{
real mu[N-1];
for (n in 1:(N-1))
mu[n] <- theta[n] + alpha[Ind[n]];

tail(y, N-1) ~ normal(mu, sigma[1]);
}

The brackets will make mu a local variable. Or you can declare
it at the top of the model block.

- Bob
